L3145@P36: Appendix B. Germs of complex analytic spaces
L3146@P36: In this section we use germs to extend the category of complex analytic spaces
L3147@P36: to include certain Stein compacts. This will be used later to establish a tight connection between the scheme theory and complex analytic geometry. In particular,
L3148@P36: this is needed to develop a relative GAGA theory.
L3149@P36: B.1. Semianalytic sets. We follow the setup of Frisch [Fri67]. A subset X of an
L3150@P36: analytic space X is called semianalytic if its local germs belong to the minimal class
L3151@P36: of germs, stable under finite unions and complements, generated by inequalities of
L3152@P36: the form f(x) < 0 for real analytic f, see [Fri67, p. 120]. It is called a Stein if X
L3153@P36: has a fundamental system of neighborhood of Stein subspaces of X, see [Fri67, p.
L3154@P36: 123].
L3155@P36: B.2. The category of germs. A germ of a complex analytic space (or, simply, a
L3156@P36: germ) is a pair (X, X) consisting of an analytic space X and a semianalytic subset
L3157@P36: X ⊂ X. We call X the support of (X, X) and we call X a representative of (X, X).
L3158@P36-37: Sometimes, we will use the shorter notation X = (X, X).38 D. ABRAMOVICH AND M. TEMKIN
L3159@P37: A morphism φ: (X, X) → (Y, Y ) consists of a neighborhood X
L3160@P37: ′ of X and an
L3161@P37: analytic map f : X
L3162@P37: ′ → Y taking X to Y . We say that f is a representative of φ.
L3163@P37: Note that a morphism (X, X) → (Y, Y ) is an isomorphism if it induces a bijection
L3164@P37: of X and Y and an isomorphism of their neighborhoods.
L3165@P37: We identify an analytic space X with the germ (X, X). In particular, the category of analytic spaces becomes a full subcategory of the category of germs.
